full_judgment:
10. The meaning of irreparable loss and injury is by now well settled. Irreparable loss and injury is that which if not prevented by injunction can not be afterwards compensated by any decree. In the application for temporary/mandatory injunction particularly in paragraph 8 thereof it has been alleged that due to non-performance of the terms of the agreement by the defendant, plaintiff Samity have suffered loss of Taka 95,20,000.00 for the period from 8-5-96 to 28-5-96 and further the plaintiff Samity are incurring loss of Taka 1,20,000.00 per day. Thus the alleged loss sustained by the plaintiff does not come within the definition of irreparable loss and injury as aforesaid. 

 11. Thirdly, admittedly defendant No. 1 has served notice dated 5-5-96 or terminating the agency as per term No. 6 of the agreement. According to term No. 6, either of the parties can terminate the agreement by serving two months notice on sufficient cause. The language used in term No.6 shows that sufficient cause is at the discretion of the parties to effect such a notice. In equity a Court does not decree performance of an agreement in a case where parties are entitled to revoke or dissolve the agreement. Underlying reasoning is that it will be idle to pass a decree which can be undone by the other party lawfully. Clause (d) of section 21 of the Specific Relief Act states that a contract which in its nature is revocable cannot be specifically enforced.
